**Organization:** The Midtown Association (MA) is a non\-profit organization that is making Midtown the center for culture, creativity and vibrancy in Sacramento’s urban core. We were recently selected by our team and the Sacramento Business Journal as one of the Best Places to Work in Sacramento.

 **Our Culture and Values:** Our small but mighty team is fast\-paced, creative, and mission\-driven. We value:


* Integrity: High standards and personal accountability
* Responsiveness: Empathetic, thorough service to all stakeholders
* Growth: Personal, team, and organizational growth celebrated often
* Collaboration: Helping others succeed as part of a collective mission
* Resiliency \& Resourcefulness: Adaptability in a changing environment
* Efficiency Through Technology: Tech\-driven transparency and results

Our modern, open\-concept office is surrounded by more than 20 restaurants, coffee shops, and cultural amenities. Our team enjoys a smart casual/business dress code.  



  

**Position Summary and Requirements:** The key measures of success for the Director are (a) lead an effective strategic communications and advocacy strategy for Midtown and the organization including organizational communications, stakeholder and media relations, electronic and digital communications, community committees, advocacy efforts, and presentations that results in Midtown’s programs and initiatives success, (b) increase visits to and sales tax in the Midtown district through effective story telling, (c) advise internal teams and community partners on efforts to enhance and preserve the reputation and investment value of the district, (d) collaborating effectively across Admin, Communications, Events, Placemaking, and Clean and Safe teams to align communication efforts with organizational priorities. **What is a Midtown Association Director**? Directors have successful supervisory experience of staff and consultants, are able to act as the staff support to committees of board members and expert community members, are politically astute, drive program budget development and deliver program projects within developed budgets, operate with high integrity to uphold company policies, and can plan program performance to generate specific outcomes. Directors should have no less than ten years of professional experience in a relevant area and a bachelor’s degree in a relevant area of study.

* Be a politically astute, strategic thinker with a proven ability to design a successful public affairs and communications strategy.
* Possess an awareness of Sacramento’s economic and political landscape, being able to understand the objectives and opinions of a diverse group of stakeholders, colleagues, and community members.
* Be experienced in developing both organizational and campaign\-specific communications plans.
* Be an effective people manager to guide high\-performing staff and consultants to set and achieve team and individual goals and objectives within the communication strategy as well as personal and professional development goals.
* Be an effective collaborator with other program leaders to ensure their projects and programs are effectively integrated into the communications strategy.
* Be an excellent written, verbal, and visual storyteller to guide and protect the Explore Midtown brand voice, messaging coherence, and identity within the communications strategy.

* Be experienced in navigating crises as a part of a team, with the ability to display tact and demonstrate discretion when dealing with sensitive matters or difficult subjects.
* Be in a continuous improvement mindset to look for new opportunities to grow and shape the organization.
* Be familiar with digital tools and tactics, including SEO/SEM best practices, Facebook Business Manager, Google Ads, geofencing, website management, and keyword advertising.

**Position Overview**


Reporting to the Executive Director, the Managing Director of Marketing \& Communications (MarCom) is a strategic leader who proactively creates and elevates our messaging and communication strategy to raise awareness of our mission, expand our media presence, and deepen connection among key stakeholders. The Managing Director of MarCom will oversee and support the implementation of City Year’s branding strategy in Los Angles to ensure consistent coherent representation of CYLA’s impact across all departments and communication outlets, including CYLA’s social media platforms. As a member of the City Year Los Angeles Senior Leadership Team (SLT), they will be a highly effective storyteller who can bring to life City Year’s impact. They will manage the Sr. Marketing \& Communications Manager.  

  

This position is perfect for someone who is entrepreneurial with proven communications experience, and who is a proactive leader, creative, strategic thinker, and willing to challenge old conventions to push beyond traditional communications.  

  

The ideal candidate cares deeply about addressing systemic inequities in education and can represent CYLA powerfully in community spaces. This individual should be able to operate at a high level, able to think about the big picture and the best way to communicate and engage the community at large.  

  

City Year values and continuously works to build an equitable and inclusive culture where people with diverse lived experiences feel they belong.**Job Description**

**Responsibilities**

**Marketing \& Communications Strategy**

* In partnership with the Executive Director, Board Members, SLT, and the City Year headquarters’ teams, lead the development and implementation of a strategic and diversified Marketing \& Communications plan that meets current goals and anticipates future needs and growth objectives.
* Lead 20th Anniversary Board Committee to create and implement milestone Marketing \& Communication strategy.
* Develop clear communication cascade and strategy for disseminating communications to external audiences (e.g., communication medium, audience, etc.)
* Leverage and amplify the national organizational Marketing, Communications, and Creative teams’ content, strategy, and materials to advance the Los Angeles and organizational impact.
* In collaboration with the Managing Director of Development, create the strategy, messaging, and design of all fundraising communications, including event invitations, sponsorship decks, event programs, donor\-facing videos, and stage remarks.
* In collaboration with the Impact team, analyze ongoing program data to support storytelling of the impact of our work throughout the year.
* Develop and implement strategic initiatives aimed at building awareness of CYLA locally by leveraging LA assets that strengthen the brand.
* Collaborate with Managing Director of Government Relations to position City Year in the community and with public officials to help build awareness of our work and garner support.
* Deepen City Year Los Angeles’ presence and reputation in communities where we serve.

**Senior Leadership \& Staff Management**

* As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, develop Los Angeles site strategic plan and lead implementing the site’s local operating plan.
* Work with SLT and national leaders to understand priorities and business goals and develop strategies to meet the organization’s needs.
* Serve as a strategic advisor to SLT on narrative positioning, reputational considerations, and public\-facing communications including major fundraising moments and campaigns.
* Leverage Board where appropriate to reach departmental and site\-wide marketing \& communication goals.

* Ensure professional accountability with direct report and team through clear expectations, weekly check\-ins, and formal performance reviews.

* Support content development for City Year Los Angeles’ Instagram, Facebook and Twitter accounts, blog, E\-newsletter, eBlasts, and publication of all other electronic communications.
* Ensure consistency of messaging within CYLA by sharing expectations, tone, and content with other departments.

**Content Strategy \& Storytelling**

* Oversee creation of all communications collateral, including multi\-media, videos, website, media materials, and other items as needed.
* Oversee the creation of annual impact reports tailored for individual donors, foundations, program sponsors, and team sponsors to ensure meaningful stewardship and donor recognition.
* Support development and core messaging for all major fundraising initiatives, including the annual Spring Break Gala, ensuring alignment across all communications, collateral, and event deliverables.

YWCA Greater Los Angeles (GLA) is dedicated to eliminating racism, empowering women and promoting peace, justice, freedom and dignity for all. We provide direct services, empowerment programming, and advocacy to support marginalized individuals and families, especially women and girls of color, while working to challenge structural barriers to equity.

**Position Overview**


The Chief Program Officer (CPO) is responsible for overseeing the delivery of high\-quality programs throughout Los Angeles. Collaborating closely with the Executive Leadership team, the CPO takes charge of program delivery, devises integrated strategies to advance the YWCA of Greater Los Angeles' mission, ensures program deliverables, and supervises the day\-to\-day activities of the program staff.


With a primary accountability for ensuring that women of all ages receive supportive services from a well\-coordinated and proficient team, the CPO also oversees contract management, ensuring financial alignment with core priorities. Additionally, the CPO ensures that the impact of services is accurately reported, represented, and effectively communicated.


The CPO actively engages staff in developing consistent, innovative, and robust service models. This involves expanding results in a cost\-effective manner, all while prioritizing the long\-term professional growth and training of the staff dedicated to delivering comprehensive services.

**Duties \& Responsibilities**

* Plans, develops, and implements program activities aligning with the strategic plan to achieve desired outcomes for the organization.
* Conducts assessments for target populations/communities, providing recommendations for ongoing and new programs.
* Develops and maintains productive relationships with community groups, social service organizations, and public/private entities interfacing with YWCA GLA programs.
* Participates in the development and revision of standard operating procedures related to Program Services.
* Ensures compliance with all licensing requirements, especially in Child Development, and monitor the Child Development Division.
* Ensures appropriate staffing levels to achieve outcomes and maintains high\-quality service delivery.
* Provides direction and supervision to Program Managers and Directors, communicating job objectives, and conducting performance planning and appraisals.
* Facilitates training and credentialing for staff and interns.
* Collaborates with Development Department and Program staff to develop and submit grant proposals to public and private sector funders.
* Oversees the development and management of program budgets, ensuring full utilization of financial resources available to each program.
* Authorizes and approves budgeted, direct costs, and equipment expenditures for all programs.
* Submits quarterly status reports to the Chief Executive Officer and Board of Directors on all programs, including service levels, program performance measures, expenditures/balances, and staffing levels.
* Regularly meets and collaborates with the Finance Department to ensure accurate execution and reporting of program expenditures.
* Monitors and adheres to all grant specifications, ensuring timely reporting and evaluation.


Minimum Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree (BS/BA) in Social Work or a related field. Emphasis on administration and community organizing is preferred.
* Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) or Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) highly desired.
* Minimum of five (5\) years of experience managing multiple programs in a medium to large nonprofit organization, public agency, or related industry.
* Demonstrated minimum five (5\) years of experience working with diverse community groups, partnerships, and staff.
* Possesses management and program development skills, including demonstrated experience in program evaluation.
* In\-depth knowledge of budgets and allocations is required.
* Must have experience with government grant processes.

Los Angeles, CA 90015


This is not a remote position.

jobs.description:
**Chief Development Officer****About the Client** Our client is a mission\-driven nonprofit focused on civic education and democracy\-building, engaging youth and communities in civic learning nationwide. As the organization scales its impact, they're building out a modern development function to match their ambitions — creating a brand\-new C\-suite role to lead the charge.


**About the Role** This is a newly created, first\-ever Chief Development Officer position, reporting directly to the President \& CEO and overseeing a team of 2 (including a Sr. Director of Advancement). The CDO will own org\-wide development strategy, leading the transformation from a grant\-centered funding model to a diversified, relationship\-driven philanthropy operation spanning major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, alumni engagement, and institutional funding. This is a hands\-on leadership role — the CDO will personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors and close six\- and seven\-figure gifts, while also building the systems, team, and board engagement needed for long\-term fundraising growth.


**Responsibilities**

* Own org\-wide development strategy and drive an initial $600K–$1M in annual contributed revenue, with sustained year\-over\-year growth
* Lead the shift from grant\-centered fundraising to a diversified, relationship\-driven philanthropy model (major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, alumni, institutional)
* Personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors; close six\- and seven\-figure gifts; run moves management and stewardship
* Build alumni\-engagement pathways to convert former program participants into an active donor community
* Lead and mentor the development team; set KPIs, dashboards, and forecasting; ensure disciplined CRM (Salesforce) usage
* Serve as the CEO's fundraising partner and drive board engagement in donor cultivation and solicitation

**Requirements**

* 10\+ years of progressive nonprofit development/fundraising/advancement experience, including ownership of fundraising strategy and revenue growth
* Demonstrated success personally closing multiple six\- and seven\-figure gifts
* 5\+ years supervising development staff
* Proven ability to build a diversified development function beyond grants
* Genuine mission alignment with civic education, democracy, and/or youth civic learning

**Benefits \& Why Join**

* Ground\-floor opportunity to build and define a brand\-new C\-suite function
* Direct partnership with the CEO and board on organizational fundraising strategy
* Hybrid/remote flexibility, with HQ based in Calabasas, CA

Classics Northwest presents the Pacific Northwest's premier classical music festival experience. You are an entrepreneurial relationship\-builder who combines strong donor instincts with organizational discipline and follow\-through. The Amherst Survival Center is seeking an experienced and effective fundraising professional to lead the development program of the Center, ensuring that the organization has the financial resources to sustain and expand its critical role providing food, clothing, healthcare, and community. The Director of Development’s primary focus is individual and business giving, using a fundraising approach that celebrates our collective responsibility, community capacity, shared humanity, and dignity of all. With a current budget of $2\.1M (plus more than $2\.5M of in\-kind contributions \-\- primarily donated food), the Center is well positioned with robust community support, many long\-term relationships, and a strong reputation for providing high\-quality and effective services in an inclusive and respectful manner.  

Candidates should bring a minimum of 4 years (6\+ preferred) of fund development experience at the coordinator/manager level or higher, with primary duties related to individual fundraising; demonstrated track record of meeting/exceeding fundraising goals; and exemplary written and verbal communication skills. Candidates with direct experience cultivating and securing major gifts (5\-figure \+) strongly preferred. Candidates must be highly organized, have strong attention to detail, and be able to tell our story in clear, compelling ways that center the dignity and humanity of all Amherst Survival Center community members.

***\*Important note:*** *While we would strongly prefer to hire for this role at the Director level, we will also consider candidates with less experience at the Manager level ($66,500\-71,500/year) for an adjusted position. Candidates should indicate in their cover letter if they are interested in being considered for a Manager\-level role.* 

**Description:** The Director of Development is responsible for leading the development program of the Amherst Survival Center, holding primary accountability for meeting annual fundraising goals; and doing so with a fundraising approach that lifts our collective responsibility, community capacity, shared humanity, and dignity of all. The Director of Development’s primary focus is individual and business/organizational giving, including annual giving, major giving, planned giving, fundraising events, and sponsorship. The Director of Development is a member of the organization’s leadership team, and has the lead responsibility for the creation, implementation, and assessment of the Center’s development strategies. The Director of Development leads the execution of the development plan, working in partnership with the Executive Director and Development Committee, and with support from the Development Associate.

**Hours/classification:** This is a full time, exempt (salaried) position. The schedule is generally weekdays, with some evening and weekend availability required for events. Limited remote work may be feasible.

**Essential Responsibilities:** 

**Development Strategy** 

* Envision, design and implement short and long\-term development and communication strategy to enhance visibility and financial support of the organization, increasing fundraising capacity.
* Ensure development strategy is both effective at achieving revenue goals and in alignment with our approach, lifting our collective responsibility, community capacity, shared humanity, and dignity of all.
* Evaluate fundraising activities (appeals, events, sponsorship, etc.) for effectiveness and improvement. Identify, assess, and implement new or different activities and approaches as appropriate to meet goals for increased revenue.
* Serve as an active member of the organization’s leadership team, ensuring continuity between operational and developmental strategy, feasibility of operational goals, and integration of development priorities throughout the organization.
* Engage staff, Board, and other stakeholders in building a shared, values\-aligned approach to fundraising—fostering a culture of philanthropy rooted in dignity, authenticity, and shared purpose.

**Donor Cultivation, Stewardship \& Solicitation** 

* Develop relationships with donors and stakeholders, inspiring support of the Center.
* Direct ongoing donor stewardship program, including coordinating the donor stewardship efforts of the Development Committee.
* Lead donor prospecting efforts. Identify, research, and cultivate new major gift prospects. Develop and implement moves management system.
* Direct and support donor meetings with the Executive Director, and/or Board and Committee Members.
* Direct and support stewardship of major donors and special project donors with the Executive Director.
* Ensure timely and personalized acknowledgement of donors.
* Envision, manage and execute donor appeals and special campaigns, including writing and developing associated materials.
* Manage donor database (currently Donor Perfect).
* Ensure adherence to appropriate processes for gift handling, recording, and acknowledgement.
* Ensure we have effective development\-related collateral.

**Fundraising Events** 

* Lead event strategy\-\- planning, coordinating and executing in partnership with development or event committees.
* Serve as staff liaison to event planning committees and coordinate event volunteers, either directly, or overseeing Development Associate in this capacity, depending on the event.

* Serve as staff liaison to the Development Committee.
* Plan and facilitate effective Development Committee meetings in partnership with the committee chair.
* Provide training, support, and follow up to Development Committee members to increase their effectiveness.

new_jobs.description:
**Department:** Social Work
  

**Reports To:** Department Chair
  

**FLSA:** Exempt  

  

  

Marian University is a Catholic applied liberal arts community that values diverse spiritual traditions. Sponsored by the Congregation of the Sisters of St. Agnes, Marian University engages students in the education of the whole person. We embrace justice and compassion to transform lives for professional service and leadership in the global community.


Marian University invites applicants for the Program Director and Assistant Professor of Social Work position, starting in August 2026\. Successful candidates will have a strong commitment to undergraduate education, student engagement, and service to the college and community. Marian University is an institution that values innovative teaching, advising, and mentoring. All faculty members participate in advising and mentoring, as well as other related duties as assigned.


Teaching responsibilities include contributing to our adult accelerated and online programs, as demand requires. Candidates should exhibit skill and enthusiasm in teaching undergraduates and developing innovative experiential learning opportunities in the surrounding community and be willing to participate in all phases of the program, departmental, college, and university activities. The normal credit load is 12 credits per semester (fall \& spring semesters). Program Director duties include a three (3\) credit course release.


**Primary Responsibilities:**


* Teach courses throughout the curriculum in the CSWE\-accredited undergraduate Social Work Program in on\-campus, online, and hybrid Examples include Ethics and Professional Behavior, Introduction to Social Work, and Generalist Practice. Social Work Policy \& Advocacy, and Research Methods.
* Schedule program course offerings, including identifying staffing of the courses.
* Recruit and mentor program faculty, including adjunct instructors, as needed.
* Coordinate the assessment of student learning in program curriculum and report data to university staff and accreditors.
* Involvement in active scholarship.
* Engage in professional or academic activities in campus\-based, local, regional, or broader communities to make a positive impact and advance the recognition and reputation of Marian University.
* Actively engages in developing and maintaining relationships in the social work practice community to enhance internship and placement opportunities for our students.
* Actively participate in on\-campus and off\-campus research seminars and other collaborative professional development activities to build collaborations between and among Marian University faculty and external partners.
* Be actively involved in student advising and mentoring, assessment and assurance of learning, curriculum design and revision, and committee service at all levels of the institute.
* Assist post\-graduate relationships, networks, and establishment of external industry relations to promote programs to industry employers, secure ongoing placement channels, and initiate industry collaborations.
* Work with a culturally diverse population.
* Strictly honor the privacy, security, and confidentiality of student records and other sensitive information according to state, federal, and college regulations, policies and procedures.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications:**


* Masters in Social Work; a terminal degree in the discipline is preferred.
* Must be able to demonstrate the potential to engage in scholarly and professional activity that supports the teaching mission of the institution.
* Willingness to support the Mission and Core Values of Marian University.

**Preferred qualifications include:**


* Ph.D. in Social Work. ABD and demonstration of effective teaching experience will be considered.
* Licensure or master’s level certification preferred.
* Knowledge and experience with CSWE accreditation standards.
* Experience in criminal justice, psychology, and/or sociology is a plus, but not required.
* Experience in online learning/teaching

To apply, please submit a letter of interest, a curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy, unofficial copies of transcripts, and the names, email addresses, and telephone numbers of three references to \[email protected]. Please place “Program Director, Social Work” in the subject line of the email.


**Applications received by August 3, 2026, will receive full consideration. Review of applications will continue, thereafter, until the position is filled.**


EOE/Minorities/Females/Vet/Disabled


*Transforming lives through academic excellence, innovation and leadership. Marian University is a community committed to learning, dedicated to service and social justice, and joined together by spiritual traditions.*
